[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Equinix. Equinix Inc was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former facilities managers at Digital Equipment Corporation, per Equinix corporate history as summarized on Wikipedia, fetched this session. Equinix is headquartered in Redwood City, California, and converted to a real estate investment trust structure in January 2015, later describing itself, per Wikipedia, as a digital infrastructure company from September 2020 onward. Equinix own about page, fetched this session, states the company currently operates 281 data centers spanning metros across six continents, with more than 513,000 interconnections and more than 10,500 customers, and describes itself directly as the world digital infrastructure company. Wikipedia separately states a close but not identical figure, approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries on five continents with about 13,000 employees, as of 2025, both figures are recorded here rather than reconciled. Wikipedia own account of Equinix acquisition history lists a 2002 merger with I-STT and Pihana Pacific expanding into the Asia Pacific region, a 2007 acquisition of IXEurope that established the company European market presence, a 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about 3.8 billion dollars, its largest acquisition at that time, a 2016 purchase of 29 data centers from Verizon, a 2020 acquisition of the bare metal cloud provider Packet, and a 2021 acquisition of Main One for about 320 million dollars expanding into West Africa. Equinix trades on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol EQIX. This batch covers 11 facilities in this registry that had carried an exhausted research status, all in Europe, across Finland, Italy, Spain, and Poland, the first non United States batch researched in this campaign. Given that both the 2007 IXEurope acquisition and the 2015 TelecityGroup acquisition materially built out Equinix European footprint, either or both are plausible historical origins for some of these European facilities, but no per facility lineage to either predecessor company was found on Equinix own current facility pages fetched this session, so this batch does not assert which historical company, if either, any specific building traces back to. The remaining 45 facilities attributed to Equinix in this registry, all in the United States, were already marked complete before this session and are untouched by this batch. Equinix own dedicated page for this facility, MD6, fetched this session, gives its address as Calle Pedriza 12, Alcobendas, 28108 Madrid, Spain, noting Alcobendas is a municipality in the greater Madrid metropolitan area, though the registry own city field for this row was blank prior to this pass. The page states N plus 1 power and cooling redundancy, 230 volt and 400 volt power distribution, a minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, a 99.9999 percent or better global uptime guarantee, and sourcing from 100 percent renewable energy including solar guarantees of origin from Spain and a virtual power purchase agreement. Certifications listed include ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, LEED, and the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact. The page did not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts, nor a colocation space figure, stating that detailed specifications require contacting sales directly.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Equinix. Equinix Inc was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former facilities managers at Digital Equipment Corporation, per Equinix corporate history as summarized on Wikipedia, fetched this session. Equinix is headquartered in Redwood City, California, and converted to a real estate investment trust structure in January 2015, later describing itself, per Wikipedia, as a digital infrastructure company from September 2020 onward. Equinix own about page, fetched this session, states the company currently operates 281 data centers spanning metros across six continents, with more than 513,000 interconnections and more than 10,500 customers, and describes itself directly as the world digital infrastructure company. Wikipedia separately states a close but not identical figure, approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries on five continents with about 13,000 employees, as of 2025, both figures are recorded here rather than reconciled. Wikipedia own account of Equinix acquisition history lists a 2002 merger with I-STT and Pihana Pacific expanding into the Asia Pacific region, a 2007 acquisition of IXEurope that established the company European market presence, a 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about 3.8 billion dollars, its largest acquisition at that time, a 2016 purchase of 29 data centers from Verizon, a 2020 acquisition of the bare metal cloud provider Packet, and a 2021 acquisition of Main One for about 320 million dollars expanding into West Africa. Equinix trades on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol EQIX. This batch covers 11 facilities in this registry that had carried an exhausted research status, all in Europe, across Finland, Italy, Spain, and Poland, the first non United States batch researched in this campaign. Given that both the 2007 IXEurope acquisition and the 2015 TelecityGroup acquisition materially built out Equinix European footprint, either or both are plausible historical origins for some of these European facilities, but no per facility lineage to either predecessor company was found on Equinix own current facility pages fetched this session, so this batch does not assert which historical company, if either, any specific building traces back to. The remaining 45 facilities attributed to Equinix in this registry, all in the United States, were already marked complete before this session and are untouched by this batch. This row carried no website URL on file in the registry, unlike its 8 sibling Italy and Finland rows in this batch. This session located the operator own dedicated page for this facility by trying the same equinix.com URL pattern already on file for those siblings, substituting the facility code wa3 and the Poland and Warsaw region path segments, which resolved successfully on the first attempt. That page gives the facility address as Aleje Jerozolimskie 213, 02-222 Warsaw, Poland, in the Salomea district, the registry own city field for this row was blank prior to this pass. The page states 1,400 square meters, 15,069 square feet, of colocation space in a three storey reinforced concrete building, N plus 1 power and cooling redundancy, 30 or more hours of generator autonomy, and a 99.9999 percent or better global uptime guarantee. The page did not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts.

Equinix, Inc. is a publicly traded real estate investment trust headquartered in Redwood City, California, trading as EQIX, SEC filer CIK 1101239.

The company's own site states a global footprint of 281 data centers spanning metros across six continents, organized into Americas, Europe/Middle East/Africa, and Asia Pacific regions, with more than 513,000 interconnections between customer networks, a figure the site says exceeds its next ten competitors combined, and more than 10,500 customers. The fetched page did not include a founding year, an exact headquarters street address, a megawatt capacity total, or a dollar-denominated construction investment figure.

The registry here tracks 45 Equinix facilities across six states, California, Illinois, New Jersey, Texas, Virginia, and Washington, a narrower US footprint than the company's stated global scale, reflecting Equinix's interconnection-and-colocation business model, in which Equinix builds and operates dense network-exchange facilities in major metro cores rather than the large single-campus buildouts favored by hyperscalers such as AWS or Meta. Equinix's 513,000-plus interconnection figure is a network-density claim rather than a compute or power capacity figure, and it is not directly comparable to the facility counts or MW totals recorded for other operators in this registry.
